posts.title: GitHub PRs are slow. Keep shipping anyway.
posts.description: The issue is ready, the code is ready, and then the PR page spins. A check stays queued. A webhook arrives late. The review that should have taken ten minutes turns into an afternoon of refreshing GitHub and wondering which part of the pipeline is actually broken.

posts.title: AI code quality: Ship fast without the fires
posts.description: The October 2025 DynamoDB disruption spread through AWS after a race condition in automated DNS management erased the service’s regional endpoint. Its published cause was an automation defect, not AI-written code. That distinction matters. If we blame every outage on an LLM, we miss the specific mechanisms that made the outage possible.

posts.title: Long-running coding agents: When to stop and split
posts.description: I have written about Herdr as a place to see all the agents and about why I give spaces, tabs, and panes specific jobs. A multiplexer helps me find the agent that is blocked on a question. It does not tell me whether the agent should still be working on that question at all.
